title: CAPACITY — DEVELOPING SUPERPOWERS
bigIdea: Giants do not create capacity. Giants reveal capacity.
openLine: Your SuperPower is not what you wish you could do. Your SuperPower is the capacity you have taken time to develop.
closeLine: Don't wait for your Goliath to start developing your sling.
declaration:
I will build in THE CAVE.
I will stand in THE COVENANT.
I will live for THE CAUSE.
I will act with COURAGE.
I will produce CONQUEST.

weeks.name: THE CAVE
weeks.rhyme:
In the cave where no one sees,
God is training hands and knees;
Lion, bear, and sling, and stone —
Competence is built alone!

weeks.name: THE COVENANT
weeks.rhyme:
I am not my height or size,
Covenant has better eyes;
Whose I am is who I'll be —
Confidence lives inside me!

weeks.name: THE CAUSE
weeks.rhyme:
Is there not a cause? There is!
Bigger than my wants and wish;
Born to answer, not applaud —
Conviction takes its cause from God!

weeks.name: THE COURAGE
weeks.rhyme:
Not one stone stays in my hand,
I will run, I will not stand;
Move while shaking — take the shot!
Courage uses what I've got!

weeks.name: THE CONQUEST
weeks.rhyme:
Giant falls and armies rise,
Someone else believes and tries;
Not just blessed — I'm sent to be
God's own answer. Come and see!

guardrail: The SuperPower is developed by the child; the victory is delivered by God. David developed a sling. God delivered the giant. Both are true, and the order matters: "the LORD saveth not with sword and spear: for the battle is the LORD's" (1 Samuel 17:47).
christThread: David is the shadow, not the hero of 1 Samuel 17: a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ (Colossians 2:17). The children are told they stand behind a greater David who has already won, and that is why they can walk into 2026/2027 with capacity.

days.title: Hidden Before Heard
days.declaration: I will develop privately until I can deliver publicly.

scripture.text: And Samuel said unto Jesse, Are here all thy children? And he said, There remaineth yet the youngest, and, behold, he keepeth the sheep.

days.hook: Somebody in this family is missing — and the prophet of God refuses to start until he arrives. Have you ever been the empty chair?
days.story: David was not even invited when Samuel came. Never despise hidden seasons.

points.head: Being left out is not being left behind.
points.body: Seven sons were presented to a prophet and nobody sent for David. God stopped the entire ceremony until the forgotten one arrived.

points.head: Hidden is not the same as forgotten.
points.body: He was in a field, not in disgrace. God knew the address.

points.head: The anointing came before the crown.
points.body: Where you are is not who you are.

mirrors.ot: Joseph — youngest, sold, forgotten in a pit and a prison, while God wrote “Prime Minister” over him (Genesis 37; 41:41).
mirrors.nt: “Let no man despise thy youth; but be thou an example of the believers” (1 Timothy 4:12).

days.christ: Jesus grew up in Nazareth — the town people asked, “Can any good thing come out of Nazareth?” (John 1:46); “he is despised and rejected of men” (Isaiah 53:3). If they overlooked the Saviour of the world, being overlooked cannot disqualify you.
days.challenge: Write your name on a card. Underneath, write one thing God has said about you that people cannot see yet. Keep it in your school bag all September.
days.prayer: What is in your heart today that only God can see — and are you glad He can see it? (1 Samuel 16:7)
days.centralTruth: Being left out is not being left behind.
days.codeLine: Hidden is not the same as forgotten.

quiz.q: How many sons were presented to the prophet before David was sent for?
Where was David when the prophet came?
What did God do when the forgotten one had not yet arrived?
options: He sent Saul to fetch him

days.title: Faithful With Sheep

scripture.text: But David went and returned from Saul to feed his father's sheep at Bethlehem.

days.hook: One of these is the reason you will ever get the other. Guess which one comes first.
days.story: Before David managed a nation, he managed sheep. Your current assignment is training for your next one.

points.head: He went back.
points.body: He had been in a palace and he still went back to the sheep. Competence does not get offended by small work.

points.head: “Those few sheep” was a real assignment.
points.body: Eliab later said it as an insult (17:28). God called it training.

points.head: Small things are the entrance exam.
points.body: “He chose David also his servant, and took him from the sheepfolds” (Psalm 78:70). Not around them. From them.

mirrors.ot: Ruth gleaning in a corner of a field she did not own — and that ordinary field placed her in the family line of Christ (Ruth 2:2–3; Matthew 1:5).
mirrors.nt: “He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much” (Luke 16:10).

days.christ: Jesus spent about thirty years in a carpenter's shop and about three in public ministry — ten times more hidden faithfulness than public ministry. And He is “the good shepherd” who “giveth his life for the sheep” (John 10:11). He is not asking you to do anything He has not already done.
days.challenge: Pick the small duty at home you usually avoid. Do it today, unasked and unannounced.
days.prayer: Name the “few sheep” God has given you this season. Have you been feeding them? (Luke 16:10)
days.centralTruth: Small things are the entrance exam.
days.codeLine: Small things are the entrance exam.

quiz.q: Where did David go back to after his time in Saul's presence?
How did Eliab use the words “those few sheep”?
According to the day, what are small things?

days.title: The Lion Lesson

scripture.text: And David said unto Saul, Thy servant kept his father's sheep, and there came a lion, and a bear, and took a lamb out of the flock:

days.hook: Nobody clapped. Nobody filmed it. Nobody even knew. And it is the reason Goliath died.
days.story: David learned courage fighting what nobody celebrated. Small battles build big capacity.

points.head: The lion came for what he was carrying.
points.body: It took a lamb out of the flock. Attacks often target your assignment, not just you.

points.head: He went after it himself.
points.body: No report, no negotiation, no waiting for reinforcements. Competence deals with what is in front of it.

points.head: Nobody clapped.
points.body: There was no crowd, no camera, no prize. That is exactly why it counted.

mirrors.ot: Samson tore a lion in a vineyard with nobody watching (Judges 14:5–6) — a private victory before a public deliverance.
mirrors.nt: “Your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about... whom resist stedfast in the faith” (1 Peter 5:8–9).

days.christ: There is a Lion who fights for us — “the Lion of the tribe of Juda hath prevailed” (Revelation 5:5). David fought one; we belong to one. Every private battle you win, you win on His strength.
days.challenge: Name one “lion” — a habit, a fear, a temptation that keeps stealing from you. Tell God about it tonight, by name.
days.prayer: What has been taken from you that God wants you to go back and recover? (1 Peter 5:8–9)
days.centralTruth: Every private battle you win, you win on His strength.
days.codeLine: Competence deals with what is in front of it.

quiz.q: What did the lion take?
options: A lamb out of the flock

quiz.q: Who went after the lion?
What was true of the fight with the lion?
options: It was reported to the king

days.title: The Bear Lesson

scripture.text: And I went out after him, and smote him, and delivered it out of his mouth:

days.hook: Lion. Bear. Giant. God never sends the giant first.
days.story: One victory became preparation for another. Every challenge can become training.

points.head: God repeats a lesson until the lesson is in you.
points.body: The lion taught him. The bear proved he had learned.

points.head: He recovered what was taken.
points.body: “I went out after him, and smote him, and delivered it out of his mouth.” God builds recoverers, not just survivors.

points.head: The second one was bigger and he was not afraid.
points.body: That is the definition of growing capacity: the next thing is harder and it no longer frightens you.

mirrors.ot: Moses given two signs at the burning bush — the rod and the hand — so the first would be believed (Exodus 4:1–9).
mirrors.nt: “Who delivered us from so great a death, and doth deliver: in whom we trust that he will yet deliver us” (2 Corinthians 1:10) — past, present, future, one God.

days.christ: Jesus was tested three times in the wilderness before He preached one sermon (Matthew 4:1–11), and returned “in the power of the Spirit” (Luke 4:14). Private test, then public power. Always that order.
days.challenge: Start your lion-and-bear page — write down one hard thing God has already brought you through. Add to it all month.
days.prayer: What has God already delivered you from that you have stopped thanking Him for? (1 Samuel 17:37)
days.centralTruth: God repeats a lesson until the lesson is in you.
days.codeLine: God never sends the giant first.

quiz.q: How many animals had David fought before the giant?
What did David recover from the bear's mouth?
What is the lion-and-bear page for?
options: Recording hard things God has already brought you through

days.title: Practise Your Sling

scripture.text: And he took his staff in his hand, and chose him five smooth stones out of the brook, and put them in a shepherd's bag which he had, even in a scrip; and his sling was in his hand: and he drew near to the Philistine.

days.hook: Now imagine doing this ten thousand times before anybody is watching. That is the entire difference between David and me.
days.story: David's weapon worked because he had used it before. Develop your gift until it becomes dependable. Later, in the cave of Adullam (1 Samuel 22:1–2), four hundred men in distress, in debt and discontented came to David there, and that cave produced his mighty men.

points.head: A sling is only a weapon in a practised hand.
points.body: In an untrained hand it is a piece of leather. The tool is not the SuperPower — the developed tool is.

points.head: Dependable beats impressive.
points.body: David's sling was not the most powerful weapon in that valley. It was the most reliable one he had.

points.head: You cannot practise during the fight.
points.body: Whatever you have not developed before the giant will not be available in front of the giant.

mirrors.ot: “What is that in thine hand?” — a shepherd's rod, used daily for forty years, became the rod of God (Exodus 4:2).
mirrors.nt: “Strong meat belongeth to them that are of full age, even those who by reason of use have their senses exercised” (Hebrews 5:14). Use is what makes it strong.

days.christ: “Though he were a Son, yet learned he obedience by the things which he suffered” (Hebrews 5:8) — so we have a High Priest “touched with the feeling of our infirmities” (Hebrews 4:15). Jesus was proved in real conditions so that He can help you in yours.
days.challenge: Name one gift God has given you. Commit to practising it for fifteen minutes a day, every day, to the end of September.
days.prayer: Which of your gifts have you never actually developed? (Hebrews 5:14)
days.centralTruth: Dependable beats impressive.
days.codeLine: Dependable beats impressive.

quiz.q: When is a sling only a piece of leather, according to the day?
What made David's sling work in that valley?
options: It was the most powerful weapon
It was the most reliable one he had

quiz.q: When can you not practise, according to the day?

days.title: THE CAVE · Competence
days.declaration: I will develop privately until I can deliver publicly.

scripture.text: For who hath despised the day of small things?

points.head: Chant
points.body: Stanza 1, three times, with actions.

points.head: Both lines together
points.body: Teach the open and close lines until the children can finish them.

points.head: Recap round
points.body: Five children, one sentence each on Days 1–5.

points.head: Declaration together
points.body: “I will develop privately until I can deliver publicly.”

points.head: Testimony slot
points.body: Who did a good thing nobody found out about? Now they may tell.

points.head: The gift roll-call
points.body: Go round the room — every child names the one gift they are practising for fifteen minutes a day. Write them all up somewhere visible. This is the spine of the whole month.

points.head: Expect this question
points.body: “How long do I have to stay hidden?” Answer honestly: until God moves you, and He is never late. The cave is not punishment.

points.head: Parents
points.body: Name one hidden faithfulness you have noticed in your child this week — out loud, in front of them.

points.head: Look ahead
points.body: “Next week we find out where David's confidence actually came from. It was not his size.”

days.prayer: What small thing are you tempted to despise? (Zechariah 4:10)
days.centralTruth: The cave is not punishment.
days.codeLine: who hath despised the day of small things?

days.title: Who Are You?
days.declaration: I know who I am, whose I am, and what God has put inside me.

scripture.text: I will praise thee; for I am fearfully and wonderfully made. Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee.

days.hook: Write who you are. Not your name — who you ARE.
days.story: Your capacity begins with identity.

points.head: You were made on purpose, with purpose.
points.body: “I will praise thee; for I am fearfully and wonderfully made” (Psalm 139:14). Nothing about you is an accident.

points.head: God knew you before anybody named you.
points.body: “Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee” (Jeremiah 1:5). Your identity is older than your birthday.

points.head: Capacity is discovered, not invented.
points.body: You are not trying to become somebody. You are learning what God already put in you.

mirrors.ot: Gideon was hiding in a winepress when the angel called him “thou mighty man of valour” (Judges 6:12). God named him by his future, not his hiding place.
mirrors.nt: “We are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus unto good works, which God hath before ordained that we should walk in them” (Ephesians 2:10).

days.christ: Jesus knew exactly who He was — “I know whence I came, and whither I go” (John 8:14) — and He is the one who gives us our identity: “as many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of God” (John 1:12). You do not find yourself. You find Him, and He tells you who you are.
days.challenge: Write three true sentences that begin “I am…” — using only what God's word says about you.
days.prayer: Do you believe you were made on purpose? What would change today if you did? (Psalm 139:14)
days.centralTruth: Capacity is discovered, not invented.
days.codeLine: Capacity is discovered, not invented.

quiz.q: What did God know before anybody named you?
options: You, before you were formed in the belly

quiz.q: According to the day, how is capacity received?
Where was Gideon hiding when the angel named him?

days.title: Whose Are You?

scripture.text: Know ye that the LORD he is God: it is he that hath made us, and not we ourselves; we are his people, and the sheep of his pasture.

days.hook: No name on it. No owner. So anybody can pick it up — and anybody can throw it away. Do you know who owns you?
days.story: You belong to God before you belong to any crowd.

points.head: He made us, not we ourselves.
points.body: “Know ye that the LORD he is God: it is he that hath made us, and not we ourselves; we are his people, and the sheep of his pasture.”

points.head: Belonging settles you.
points.body: A child who knows whose they are stops auditioning for every crowd.

points.head: Ownership means covering.
points.body: If you are His sheep, He is your shepherd — and shepherds fight lions.

mirrors.ot: “Fear not: for I have redeemed thee, I have called thee by thy name; thou art mine” (Isaiah 43:1).
mirrors.nt: “Ye are not your own... for ye are bought with a price” (1 Corinthians 6:19–20).

days.christ: “My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me... neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand” (John 10:27–28). The price of your belonging was His blood. That is how secure your identity is.
days.challenge: Notice one moment today when you were tempted to change who you are to fit in. Choose differently.
days.prayer: Whose approval have you been working hardest for this year? (Psalm 100:3)
days.centralTruth: You belong to God before you belong to any crowd.
days.codeLine: You belong to God before you belong to any crowd.

quiz.q: Who made us, according to the day's reading?
options: He made us, not we ourselves

quiz.q: What does belonging do for a child, according to the day?
options: It settles them and stops them auditioning for every crowd
It replaces the need for prayer

quiz.q: What do shepherds do, in the day's point about covering?

days.title: Uncircumcised Philistine

scripture.text: And David spake to the men that stood by him, saying, What shall be done to the man that killeth this Philistine, and taketh away the reproach from Israel? for who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should defy the armies of the living God?

days.hook: “NINE FEET TALL.” “NO COVENANT.” Both of these are true about Goliath. One of them is about to get him killed. Which one?
days.story: David interpreted Goliath through covenant.

points.head: David measured Goliath against God, not himself.
points.body: Against David, Goliath was huge. Against “the armies of the living God,” he was nothing.

points.head: Covenant is the real measurement.
points.body: His confidence was not in his size but in his side.

points.head: Naming things correctly disarms them.
points.body: Everyone else said “the champion.” David said “this uncircumcised Philistine” — a man with no covenant and therefore no covering.

mirrors.ot: Jonathan, two men against a garrison: “there is no restraint to the LORD to save by many or by few” (1 Samuel 14:6).
mirrors.nt: “Greater is he that is in you, than he that is in the world” (1 John 4:4).

days.christ: We are in a better covenant — “a surety of a better testament” (Hebrews 7:22) — sealed by Christ's own blood. At the cross He “spoiled principalities and powers... triumphing over them in it” (Colossians 2:15). Your giants are already-defeated enemies still making noise.
days.challenge: Write your giant's name. Beside it write: “compared to the living God, you are ______.” Fill it in truthfully.
days.prayer: Are you measuring your problem against yourself, or against God? (1 John 4:4)
days.centralTruth: Covenant is the real measurement.
days.codeLine: Covenant is the real measurement.

quiz.q: Against whom was Goliath huge?
options: Against the armies of the living God

quiz.q: Where was David's confidence, according to the day?
What did David call Goliath?

days.title: Don't Wear Saul's Armour

scripture.text: And Saul armed David with his armour, and he put an helmet of brass upon his head; also he armed him with a coat of mail.

days.hook: Somebody is dressing you like this right now. And you are saying thank you.
days.story: Don't lose yourself trying to become somebody else.

points.head: Saul dressed David like Saul.
points.body: “And Saul armed David with his armour.” People will always try to reproduce themselves in you.

points.head: What protects one person can paralyse another.
points.body: The armour was not bad. It was not his.

points.head: “I cannot go with these” is a complete sentence.
points.body: Said respectfully, to a king — and then he took it off. Confidence knows how to decline.

mirrors.ot: Aaron's garments were made “for glory and for beauty” and fitted to specific men (Exodus 28:2–4). God has never done one-size-fits-all.
mirrors.nt: “There are diversities of gifts, but the same Spirit... the body is not one member, but many” (1 Corinthians 12:4, 14). Comparison is a category error.

days.christ: Jesus refused every costume offered Him — He would not be made king by force (John 6:15), and would not come down from the cross to prove Himself (Matthew 27:40–42). He stayed inside His own assignment, and that is precisely how we were saved.
days.challenge: Name one thing you are only doing because somebody else does it. Take it off this week.
days.prayer: Whose armour have you been wearing? (1 Corinthians 12:14)
days.centralTruth: Confidence knows how to decline.
days.codeLine: “I cannot go with these” is a complete sentence.

quiz.q: Who armed David with his armour?
What did David say about the armour?
What did David do after saying no to the armour?

days.title: Remember Your Testimony

scripture.text: The LORD that delivered me out of the paw of the lion, and out of the paw of the bear, he will deliver me out of the hand of this Philistine.

days.hook: You keep a record of everything. Where do you keep the record of what God has done?
days.story: “The LORD that delivered me…” Confidence grows when you remember what God has already done.

points.head: Testimony is the answer to intimidation.
points.body: “The LORD that delivered me out of the paw of the lion, and out of the paw of the bear, he will deliver me out of the hand of this Philistine.”

points.head: Past deliverance is a promise, not a memory.
points.body: He used a finished act of God as evidence for an unfinished one.

points.head: Keep receipts.
points.body: If you cannot recall what God has done, you will over-fear what is in front of you.

mirrors.ot: Samuel set up a stone and called it Ebenezer — “Hitherto hath the LORD helped us” (1 Samuel 7:12).
mirrors.nt: “They overcame him by the blood of the Lamb, and by the word of their testimony” (Revelation 12:11).

days.christ: The greatest testimony ever given is an empty tomb — “He is not here: for he is risen” (Matthew 28:6). David testified to a lion and a bear. We testify to a resurrection. If death could not hold Him, your giant cannot hold you.
days.challenge: Open your lion-and-bear page from Day 4. Read it out loud to one person today.
days.prayer: What is your testimony? Have you told anyone? (Revelation 12:11)
days.centralTruth: Past deliverance is a promise, not a memory.
days.codeLine: Past deliverance is a promise, not a memory.

quiz.q: Which two animals did David's testimony name?
What is past deliverance, according to the day?
What did Samuel name the stone he set up?

days.title: I Come in His Name

scripture.text: Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield: but I come to thee in the name of the LORD of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom thou hast defied.

days.hook: Raises the sling — “This was his weapon.” Raises the empty hand — “This is where his confidence was.”
days.story: David's greatest confidence wasn't his sling; it was God's Name.

points.head: Goliath came with hardware; David came with a Name.
points.body: “Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield: but I come to thee in the name of the LORD of hosts.”

points.head: He developed a sling and depended on a Name.
points.body: Both. Never one without the other — that is the whole balance of this series.

points.head: The Name settles the outcome before the fight.
points.body: “This day will the LORD deliver thee into mine hand.”

mirrors.ot: “Some trust in chariots, and some in horses: but we will remember the name of the LORD our God” (Psalm 20:7) — written by this same David, years later. He never changed weapons.
mirrors.nt: “In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth rise up and walk” (Acts 3:6). No silver, no gold — the Name.

days.christ: David borrowed that Name by faith. We know it by revelation: “God also hath highly exalted him, and given him a name which is above every name” (Philippians 2:9–11). Jesus. That is the Name your SuperPower runs on.
days.challenge: Before today's hardest moment, say out loud: “I come in the name of the Lord.”
days.prayer: What are you trusting in that is not the Name of the Lord? (Philippians 2:9–11)
days.centralTruth: The Name settles the outcome before the fight.
days.codeLine: The Name settles the outcome before the fight.

quiz.q: What did Goliath come with?
options: Hardware: a sword, a spear and a shield

quiz.q: What did David come with?
Which Name does the day's Christ point name as above every name?

days.title: THE COVENANT · Confidence
days.declaration: I know who I am, whose I am, and what God has put inside me.

scripture.text: For thou hast possessed my reins: thou hast covered me in my mother's womb... I will praise thee; for I am fearfully and wonderfully made.

points.head: Chant
points.body: Stanzas 1 + 2.

points.head: Recap round
points.body: Six children, one sentence each on Days 6–11.

points.head: Declaration together
points.body: “I know who I am, whose I am, and what God has put inside me.”

points.head: The “I am” wall
points.body: Every child reads out one of the three sentences they wrote on Day 6. Put them on a wall and leave them there all month.

points.head: Testimony slot
points.body: Who took off borrowed armour this week? Who refused to change themselves to fit in?

points.head: Expect this question
points.body: “What if I don't know what God put inside me yet?” Answer: you find it by using what is already in your hand, not by waiting for a feeling.

points.head: Parents
points.body: Affirm what is uniquely theirs about your child — not what makes them like a sibling or a cousin.

points.head: Look ahead
points.body: “Next week we find out what David was actually angry about. It wasn't the giant's size.”

days.prayer: Which of God's descriptions of you is hardest for you to believe? (Psalm 139:13–16)
days.centralTruth: You find it by using what is already in your hand, not by waiting for a feeling.
days.codeLine: using what is already in your hand

days.title: Is There Not a Cause?

scripture.text: Is there not a cause?

days.hook: A child raises a hand to volunteer; a sibling yanks it straight back down. Freeze frame. Presenter: "The first person who tries to stop you usually shares your surname."
days.story: Great people live for something bigger than themselves.

points.head: Eliab attacked his character, not his argument
points.body: "I know thy pride, and the naughtiness of thine heart." When people cannot answer you, they redefine you.

points.head: David did not defend himself; he pointed at the mission.
points.body: "Is there not a cause?" Conviction keeps the main thing the main thing.

points.head: A cause is what keeps you standing when people misread you.
points.body: Without one, criticism stops you. With one, it barely slows you down.

mirrors.ot: Nehemiah to his mockers: "I am doing a great work, so that I cannot come down" (Nehemiah 6:3).
mirrors.nt: "A prophet is not without honour, save in his own country, and in his own house" (Matthew 13:57).

days.christ: "Neither did his brethren believe in him" (John 7:5) — and yet He said, "I must work the works of him that sent me" (John 9:4). Jesus had the greatest cause ever carried, and He carried it through the doubt of His own family. His brother James later became a pillar of the church. Keep going; doubters can become disciples.
days.challenge: When someone discourages you today, do not defend yourself. Ask "is there not a cause?" — and get back to work.
days.prayer: What "great work" must you not come down from? (Nehemiah 6:3)
days.centralTruth: A cause is what keeps you standing when people misread you.
days.codeLine: Is there not a cause?

quiz.q: What did David point to instead of defending himself?
options: The mission: "Is there not a cause?"

quiz.q: According to the lesson, what does a cause do when people misread you?
What does Eliab's attack show, according to the lesson?
options: He attacked David's character, not his argument
He was David's brother by blood only

days.declaration: My life will solve a problem bigger than myself.

days.title: See the Problem
days.hook: The same shouting clip plays four times, louder each time, until it is uncomfortable. Cut to total silence. Presenter, calmly: "Forty days of that. Everybody heard him." Beat. "One boy actually looked at him."
days.story: Everybody heard Goliath. David saw a problem that could be solved.

points.head: Hearing and seeing are not the same thing.
points.body: The army heard a threat. David saw a situation with a solution in it.

points.head: Familiarity makes people stop looking.
points.body: Forty days had turned a solvable problem into normal weather. Conviction refuses to call a problem "just how things are."

points.head: Whoever sees it is usually the one sent to solve it.
points.body: If you can see it clearly and it bothers you deeply, look closer — that may be your assignment.

mirrors.ot: Nehemiah heard about broken walls and "sat down and wept, and mourned certain days" — then went and rebuilt them (Nehemiah 1:3–4). Everyone knew the walls were broken. One man saw it.
mirrors.nt: "But when he saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion on them... Pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest" (Matthew 9:36–38). Seeing came first; sending came after.

days.christ: Jesus saw what everybody else walked past — Zacchaeus in a tree (Luke 19:5), a widow's two mites (Mark 12:42), one woman in a crowded street (Mark 5:30–32). Ask Him for His eyes and He will show you your problem.
days.challenge: Walk through your day today looking, not just listening. Write down one problem you saw that nobody seems to be fixing.
days.prayer: What did you see today that others walked past? (Matthew 9:36)
days.centralTruth: Whoever sees it is usually the one sent to solve it.
days.codeLine: One boy actually looked at him.

quiz.q: What does the lesson say the army did?
options: Saw a situation with a solution in it
Prayed for the Lord of the harvest

quiz.q: What did forty days do to the problem, according to the lesson?
If a problem bothers you deeply and you can see it clearly, what does the lesson suggest?
options: Look closer, it may be your assignment

days.title: Feel the Reproach

scripture.text: Who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should defy the armies of the living God?

days.hook: Presenter sits, leans in, quiet. "I want to ask you a question almost nobody asks children." Long beat. "What makes you angry?" Beat. "Not annoyed. Angry."
days.story: David cared that Israel was being disgraced. What bothers you may point toward your assignment.

points.head: He was offended by the right thing.
points.body: "Who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should defy the armies of the living God?" Not "he might hurt me" — "he is disgracing God's people."

points.head: Holy anger is a compass.
points.body: What breaks your heart is often the map to your assignment. Pay attention to what you cannot walk past.

points.head: Feeling is not enough — David felt it and then moved.
points.body: Conviction that never becomes action is just an opinion.

mirrors.ot: Moses "spied an Egyptian smiting an Hebrew" and something in him could not accept it (Exodus 2:11–12). The instinct was right even when his method was not — and God spent forty years shaping it into deliverance.
mirrors.nt: Paul in Athens: "his spirit was stirred in him, when he saw the city wholly given to idolatry" (Acts 17:16) — and that stirring became one of the greatest sermons ever preached.

days.christ: Jesus wept over a city (Luke 19:41) and drove out the money changers because "my house shall be called the house of prayer" (Matthew 21:13). He felt the reproach on His Father's name — and then He carried the reproach Himself: "the reproaches of them that reproached thee are fallen upon me" (Romans 15:3).
days.challenge: Finish this sentence honestly: "It bothers me that ______." Bring that sentence to God tonight and ask Him what it means.
days.prayer: What breaks your heart? Have you ever asked God why? (Romans 15:3)
days.centralTruth: What breaks your heart is often the map to your assignment.
days.codeLine: Holy anger is a compass.

quiz.q: Why was David offended, according to the lesson?
options: The king had not paid him

quiz.q: What does the lesson call holy anger?
What does the lesson say about conviction that never becomes action?
options: It is the same as prayer

days.title: Ask Better Questions

scripture.text: What shall be done to the man that killeth this Philistine?

days.hook: Two children look at the same photograph. First: "That's scary." Second: "How do we fix it?" Presenter to camera: "Same picture. Same day. Two completely different futures."
days.story: "What shall be done…?" David asked different questions from everyone else.

points.head: Your questions set your direction.
points.body: The soldiers asked about the threat. David asked "What shall be done to the man that killeth this Philistine?" Same field, different future.

points.head: He asked more than once and asked around.
points.body: "And he turned from him toward another, and spake after the same manner" (17:30). He gathered information instead of absorbing atmosphere.

points.head: Outcome questions beat obstacle questions.
points.body: Faith is not the absence of the problem; it is a bigger interest in the promise.

mirrors.ot: Elisha's servant panicked at an encircling army; Elisha prayed "LORD, open his eyes" — and the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire (2 Kings 6:15–17). Same hill, better question.
mirrors.nt: Mary asked "How shall this be?" — not to doubt but to understand — and then said "be it unto me according to thy word" (Luke 1:34, 38).

days.christ: Jesus taught almost entirely in questions — "Whom say ye that I am?" (Matthew 16:15); "What wilt thou that I shall do unto thee?" (Mark 10:51). He is not afraid of your questions. He is the answer to them.
days.challenge: Take the thing worrying you most. Write one fear question and one faith question about it. Answer only the faith one.
days.prayer: What would change today if God opened your eyes to what He is doing? (2 Kings 6:17)
days.centralTruth: Your questions set your direction.
days.codeLine: Your questions set your direction.

quiz.q: Which question did David ask?
options: What shall be done to the man that killeth this Philistine?

quiz.q: How did David gather information, according to the lesson?
options: He asked more than once and asked around
He asked only once and stopped

quiz.q: What does the lesson say faith is?
options: A bigger interest in the promise

days.title: Discover Your Problem

scripture.text: Who knoweth whether thou art come to the kingdom for such a time as this?

days.hook: Presenter points straight down the lens and says nothing for four full seconds. "Today is not about David." Beat. "Today is about you. And there is only one question." Beat. "What problem has your name on it?"
days.story: What problem in your school, family, community or nation do you want to solve?

points.head: Every assignment is a problem with somebody's name on it.
points.body: David's name was on a giant. Nehemiah's was on a wall. Esther's was on a decree. Yours is on something.

points.head: Start where you already are.
points.body: Your school, your family, your street, your nation — in that order. Do not wait to be somewhere impressive.

points.head: "For such a time as this."
points.body: Esther 4:14 — you were put in this exact place, in this exact year, on purpose. 2026/2027 is not a random session for you.

mirrors.ot: Esther — "who knoweth whether thou art come to the kingdom for such a time as this?" (Esther 4:14). Her position was her assignment.
mirrors.nt: "Ye have not chosen me, but I have chosen you, and ordained you, that ye should go and bring forth fruit" (John 15:16).

days.christ: Jesus knew exactly what problem He came to solve and said it out loud in a synagogue — "The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor... to set at liberty them that are bruised" (Luke 4:18). He read His assignment publicly and then went and did it.
days.challenge: Write down one problem you want your life to help solve. School, family, community or nation. Write it clearly enough that somebody else could read it.
days.prayer: Why do you think God put you exactly where you are, in exactly this year? (Esther 4:14)
days.centralTruth: Every assignment is a problem with somebody's name on it.
days.codeLine: What problem has your name on it?

quiz.q: What does the lesson say Esther's position was?
According to the lesson, what did Jesus say His assignment was in the synagogue?
options: To preach the gospel to the poor

quiz.q: Where does the lesson say you should start?

days.title: Find Your Cause

scripture.text: David, after he had served his own generation by the will of God, fell on sleep

days.hook: Two cards held up: WHAT I DO and WHY I DO IT. Presenter tears the first one in half. "You can win at this one" — holds up the torn half — "and still waste your entire life."
days.story: Your career is what you do. Your cause is why you do it.

points.head: Career answers "what." Cause answers "why."
points.body: A career can be taken from you. A cause goes with you into every room you ever enter.

points.head: A cause outlives the person carrying it.
points.body: "David, after he had served his own generation by the will of God, fell on sleep" (Acts 13:36). That is the whole obituary — he served his generation.

points.head: Your capacity is the tool; your cause is the reason.
points.body: This is why we develop anything at all. Not so you can be amazing — so you can be useful.

mirrors.ot: Joseph's whole hard story had one sentence under it: "God did send me before you to preserve life" (Genesis 45:5). The cause explained the years.
mirrors.nt: Paul: "But none of these things move me... so that I might finish my course with joy, and the ministry, which I have received of the Lord Jesus" (Acts 20:24).

days.christ: "For this cause came I unto this hour" (John 12:27). Jesus had the greatest cause in history — to seek and save the lost — and He finished it: "It is finished" (John 19:30). Every cause a child of God carries is a branch of His.
days.challenge: Take Friday's problem and turn it into a sentence: "I want to spend my life helping to ______." Say it out loud to one adult who loves you.
days.prayer: If someone wrote one sentence about your life, what do you want it to say? (Acts 13:36)
days.centralTruth: Your capacity is the tool; your cause is the reason.
days.codeLine: Career answers what. Cause answers why.

quiz.q: Which question does a career answer, according to the lesson?
What goes with you into every room you enter?
According to Acts 13:36, how did David serve?

days.title: Discussion 3 — The Cause (Conviction)

scripture.text: But none of these things move me... so that I might finish my course with joy, and the ministry, which I have received of the Lord Jesus

points.head: Chant
points.body: Stanzas 1 + 2 + 3.

points.head: Recap round
points.body: Six children, one sentence each on Days 12–17.

points.head: Declaration together
points.body: "My life will solve a problem bigger than myself."

points.head: The cause roll-call — the centrepiece of the month
points.body: Every child who is willing stands and says their sentence: "I want to spend my life helping to ______." Write every single one down. Some children are telling you their future in that sentence — give this the time it deserves and do not rush it into the next item.

points.head: Testimony slot
points.body: Who saw a problem this week that others walked past?

points.head: Expect this question: "What if my cause is small?"
points.body: Answer: David's cause was one giant in one valley. It changed a nation. Start where your name is.

points.head: Parents
points.body: Ask your child their sentence this week and take it seriously. Do not correct it. Write it down.

points.head: Look ahead
points.body: "You can have capacity and never use it. Next week is about fear."

days.prayer: What would it take for you to finish your course with joy? (Acts 20:24)
days.centralTruth: My life will solve a problem bigger than myself.
days.codeLine: I want to spend my life helping to ______.
days.declaration: My life will solve a problem bigger than myself.

days.title: Go Towards the Giant

scripture.text: David hasted, and ran toward the army to meet the Philistine.

days.hook: Slow motion. A crowd running hard in one direction; one child running straight through them the other way. Freeze on the child. Presenter: "Everybody in this shot is behaving normally." Beat. "Except one person."
days.story: David "hasted, and ran toward the army." Courage moves toward problems.

points.head: The direction of your feet reveals the state of your heart.
points.body: Israel "fled from him, and were sore afraid" (17:24). David "hasted, and ran toward."

points.head: Courage closes the distance.
points.body: Fear negotiates from far away. Courage walks up to the thing.

points.head: Moving toward it makes it smaller.
points.body: Every problem you avoid grows in the dark. The giant was never bigger than on the day nobody approached him.

mirrors.ot: Caleb at eighty-five: "Now therefore give me this mountain" (Joshua 14:12). Ten spies fled giants; Caleb asked for their address.
mirrors.nt: Peter: "Lord, if it be thou, bid me come unto thee on the water" (Matthew 14:28–29). Eleven stayed seated. One walked.

days.christ: "He stedfastly set his face to go to Jerusalem" (Luke 9:51). Jesus ran toward the cross knowing exactly what waited there — "who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross" (Hebrews 12:2). Our courage is borrowed from His.
days.challenge: Do the one thing today you have been avoiding — the apology, the question in class, the difficult conversation. Move toward it.
days.prayer: What are you running away from that God is asking you to run toward? (Joshua 1:9)
days.centralTruth: Courage closes the distance.
days.codeLine: Go towards the giant.

quiz.q: What does the lesson say the direction of your feet reveals?
What did Israel do when they saw Goliath, according to 17:24?
options: Fled from him, and were sore afraid

quiz.q: What does the lesson say happens to a problem you avoid?

days.declaration: I will not bury what God has put inside me.

days.title: Start With What You Have

scripture.text: He chose him five smooth stones out of the brook.

days.hook: Five stones dropped into a leather bag, one at a time, in silence. Presenter looks up. "That is it. That is the entire armoury." Beat. "And it was too much — he only needed one."
days.story: A sling and five stones looked insignificant until David used them.

points.head: He used what was already in his hand.
points.body: Not what he wished he had. Not what the king offered. What he had developed.

points.head: He chose deliberately.
points.body: "He chose him five smooth stones out of the brook." Not the first five he touched. Courage is prepared, not reckless.

points.head: He took more than he needed.
points.body: One stone did it — he carried five. Preparation always carries margin.

mirrors.ot: God asked Moses, "What is that in thine hand?" — an ordinary shepherd's rod became the rod of God (Exodus 4:2).
mirrors.nt: A boy brought five loaves and two fish and Jesus fed five thousand (John 6:9–11). Small, surrendered, multiplied.

days.christ: "Take unto you the whole armour of God" (Ephesians 6:11–17) — truth, righteousness, peace, faith, salvation, the Word. Every piece of the real equipment is found in Christ. He is the armour that always fits.
days.challenge: Choose your five stones for the 2026/2027 session: five habits you will carry into the new term. Write them down and name them out loud.
days.prayer: What is already in your hand that you have been calling too small? (Exodus 4:2)
days.centralTruth: He used what was already in his hand.
days.codeLine: Start with what you have.

quiz.q: What did David use, according to the lesson?
options: What was already in his hand

quiz.q: How many stones did David carry?
How many stones did he actually need?

days.title: Stop Comparing
days.hook: Bronze armour on the left of frame, a leather sling on the right. Presenter stands between them. "One of these looked serious." Beat. "The other one won."
days.story: Saul had armour. David had a sling. Your difference may be your advantage.

points.head: Comparison always makes you the loser.
points.body: There is always someone taller, faster, richer. The moment you measure yourself against them, you stop developing yourself.

points.head: Your difference may be your advantage.
points.body: Goliath's whole battle plan assumed an armoured man walking slowly toward him. He had no answer for a fast boy with a range weapon.

points.head: God does not duplicate.
points.body: He never made two of you, so there is nothing to compare.

mirrors.ot: Gideon's three hundred, chosen precisely because they were few — "lest Israel vaunt themselves against me, saying, Mine own hand hath saved me" (Judges 7:2).
mirrors.nt: "God hath chosen the foolish things of the world to confound the wise; and... the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty" (1 Corinthians 1:27).

days.christ: When Peter compared himself to John, Jesus answered, "What is that to thee? follow thou me" (John 21:22). Comparison is a distraction from your own following. Christ has a path with your name on it, not a copy of somebody else's.
days.challenge: Notice the moment today you compare yourself to someone. Stop, and thank God for one thing He put in you instead.
days.prayer: Who have you been comparing yourself to, and what has it cost you? (1 Corinthians 1:27)
days.centralTruth: Comparison always makes you the loser.
days.codeLine: Your difference may be your advantage.

quiz.q: What did Goliath's battle plan assume, according to the lesson?
options: A fast boy with a range weapon
An armoured man walking slowly toward him

quiz.q: What does the lesson say comparison always does?
What does 'God does not duplicate' mean in the lesson?
options: He never made two of you

days.title: Courage Before Confidence

scripture.text: Let no man's heart fail because of him; thy servant will go and fight with this Philistine.

days.hook: Presenter holds out a visibly shaking hand to camera. "People think courage means this stops." Hand keeps shaking. "It doesn't." Beat. "You just move anyway."
days.story: Sometimes you have to move while you are still afraid.

points.head: Courage is not the absence of fear.
points.body: God kept telling brave people "fear not" — which means they were afraid. Fear is not disqualification.

points.head: Confidence often arrives after the first step, not before it.
points.body: David steadied the room — "Let no man's heart fail" — and then volunteered. He led with action, not with feelings.

points.head: Obedience does not wait to feel ready.
points.body: If you wait until you feel ready, you will still be waiting when the session ends.

mirrors.ot: "Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed" (Joshua 1:9) — God said it to Joshua three times in one chapter. Repeated commands answer real fear.
mirrors.nt: "God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind" (2 Timothy 1:7).

days.christ: In Gethsemane Jesus was "sore amazed, and very heavy" and prayed "let this cup pass from me: nevertheless not as I will, but as thou wilt" (Matthew 26:37–39). He felt everything — and went anyway. That is courage, and He gives it away: "In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world" (John 16:33).
days.challenge: Do one thing today while you are still nervous about it. Do not wait for the feeling to change.
days.prayer: What are you waiting to feel ready for? What if ready never comes? (2 Timothy 1:7)
days.centralTruth: Courage is not the absence of fear.
days.codeLine: Courage before confidence.

quiz.q: What does the lesson say courage is not?
What did David say to steady the room?
What does the lesson say happens if you wait until you feel ready?
options: You will still be waiting when the session ends
You will feel ready at once

days.title: Take the Shot

scripture.text: David put his hand in his bag, and took thence a stone, and slang it.

days.hook: A sling winding up, faster and faster. Freeze at full stretch. Presenter, over the frozen frame: "Every stone he ever threw in that field was for this one second." Beat. "And all of it is worth nothing until he lets go."
days.story: Eventually preparation must become action.

points.head: Preparation has an expiry point.
points.body: "David put his hand in his bag, and took thence a stone, and slang it." All the practice in the world does nothing until the hand releases.

points.head: One well-developed shot was enough.
points.body: He did not need all five. Develop deeply, then act decisively.

points.head: Unused capacity becomes buried talent.
points.body: The servant in Jesus' parable did not lose the talent — he just never used it, and that was the failure.

mirrors.ot: The four lepers at the gate of Samaria: "Why sit we here until we die?" (2 Kings 7:3–9). They moved, and the whole city ate.
mirrors.nt: "Thou wicked and slothful servant... thou oughtest therefore to have put my money to the exchangers" (Matthew 25:26–27). The sin was not losing it. The sin was burying it.

days.christ: "I must work the works of him that sent me, while it is day: the night cometh, when no man can work" (John 9:4). Jesus lived with holy urgency and finished everything He was sent to do. He is both our example and our power to act.
days.challenge: Take one action today on the cause you wrote on Day 16. One phone call, one conversation, one first step. Today.
days.prayer: What has God given you that you have buried instead of used? (Matthew 25:25–27)
days.centralTruth: Preparation has an expiry point.
days.codeLine: Take the shot.

quiz.q: What does the lesson say preparation has?
How many stones did David need, according to the lesson?
What was the failure of the servant in Jesus' parable?

days.title: Run Toward Responsibility

scripture.text: thy servant will go and fight with this Philistine.

days.hook: Two doors, marked EASY and HARD. Presenter opens EASY — an empty room. Closes it. Opens HARD — a gym full of weights. "Both doors are open to you today." Beat. "Only one of them builds you."
days.story: Capacity grows when you stop avoiding difficult assignments.

points.head: Responsibility is the gym of capacity.
points.body: Nobody grows carrying nothing. Every hard assignment you accept enlarges what you can hold.

points.head: David volunteered
points.body: "thy servant will go and fight with this Philistine." He was not drafted. He raised his hand.

points.head: The avoided assignment does not disappear; it waits.
points.body: And it is still there in the new session, only bigger.

mirrors.ot: Isaiah heard "Whom shall I send?" and answered "Here am I; send me" (Isaiah 6:8) — a volunteer, not a conscript.
mirrors.nt: "Unto whomsoever much is given, of him shall be much required" (Luke 12:48). Capacity and responsibility rise together, always.

days.christ: "Lo, I come (in the volume of the book it is written of me,) to do thy will, O God" (Hebrews 10:7). Jesus is the ultimate volunteer — He took the one responsibility nobody else could carry, and carried it to the end.
days.challenge: Volunteer for one thing this week that nobody wants to do. At home, at school, or at church.
days.prayer: What responsibility have you been avoiding, and what is it costing you? (Luke 12:48)
days.centralTruth: Responsibility is the gym of capacity.
days.codeLine: Run toward responsibility.

quiz.q: Who volunteered, according to the lesson?
What does the lesson say an avoided assignment does?
options: Waits, and is still there, only bigger

quiz.q: What does the lesson compare responsibility to?

days.title: Discussion 4 — The Courage (Use What You Have)

scripture.text: Thou wicked and slothful servant... thou oughtest therefore to have put my money to the exchangers

points.head: Chant
points.body: Stanzas 1 + 2 + 3 + 4.

points.head: Recap round
points.body: Six children, one sentence each on Days 18–23.

points.head: Declaration together
points.body: "I will not bury what God has put inside me."

points.head: The five stones
points.body: Every child who is willing says their five habits for the new session out loud. Write them up beside the "I am" wall and the cause sentences. By now that wall is the story of your whole month — photograph it.

points.head: Testimony slot
points.body: Who moved while still afraid this week? Who took a first step on their cause?

points.head: Expect this question: "What if I take the shot and I miss?"
points.body: Answer honestly: you will miss things. David carried five stones for a reason. Missing is part of developing; burying is not.

points.head: Parents
points.body: Give your child one genuinely difficult responsibility this week and let them carry it fully.

points.head: Look ahead
points.body: "Three days left. Monday, the giant finally falls — and we find out what capacity is really for."

days.prayer: Which servant are you being with what God has given you? (Matthew 25:14–29)
days.centralTruth: I will not bury what God has put inside me.
days.codeLine: I will not bury what God has put inside me.
days.declaration: I will not bury what God has put inside me.

days.title: Kill Your Giant

scripture.text: So David prevailed over the Philistine with a sling and with a stone.

days.hook: The CAVE → CONQUEST board, four panels lit, the fifth dark. Presenter walks the length of it. "Four weeks. Twenty-three days. All of it developing something nobody could see." Lights the fifth panel. "Today we find out what it was for."
days.story: Preparation must eventually produce results.

points.head: Development is measured by outcome, not effort.
points.body: "So David prevailed over the Philistine with a sling and with a stone." Four weeks of preparation, one sentence of result.

points.head: He finished it.
points.body: "There was no sword in the hand of David" (17:50) — so he used Goliath's own sword. God ends the enemy's story with the enemy's weapon.

points.head: The giant did not create David's capacity. It revealed it.
points.body: Everything that fell in that valley was developed in a field where nobody was watching. This is the big idea of the whole month — say it out loud today.

mirrors.ot: Joseph's years in a prison were revealed as preparation the moment he stood before Pharaoh (Genesis 41:14–41). Nothing wasted, all of it useful.
mirrors.nt: "I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith" (2 Timothy 4:7). Paul measured his life by what he finished.

days.christ: At Calvary the enemy's own weapon — death — became the instrument of his defeat: "that through death he might destroy him that had the power of death" (Hebrews 2:14). Jesus said "It is finished" (John 19:30). We do not fight for victory. We fight from it.
days.challenge: Finish one thing today that you started and abandoned. Do not leave it at ninety percent.
days.prayer: What is one thing you want to be able to say you finished this year? (2 Timothy 4:7)
days.centralTruth: Development is measured by outcome, not effort.
days.codeLine: Kill your giant.

quiz.q: What does the lesson say development is measured by?
What sword did David use, according to the lesson?
What did the giant do to David's capacity, according to the lesson?

days.declaration:
I will build in THE CAVE.
I will stand in THE COVENANT.
I will live for THE CAUSE.
I will act with COURAGE.
I will produce CONQUEST.

days.title: Make Others Brave

scripture.text: The men of Israel and of Judah arose, and shouted, and pursued the Philistines.

days.hook: One child stands up. Beat. A second stands. Beat. Then the entire room is on its feet. Presenter, over the top: "Nobody told them to do that." Beat. "They just needed to see it done once."
days.story: After David defeated Goliath, the entire army arose. Real capacity doesn't only change you; it changes what other people believe is possible. The echo, 2 Samuel 21:22: “These four were born to the giant in Gath, and fell by the hand of David, and by the hand of his servants.” David killed one giant; his servants killed four more. Real capacity does not just win. It reproduces.

points.head: One person's courage releases a generation.
points.body: "The men of Israel and of Judah arose, and shouted, and pursued the Philistines." They had been in that valley forty days. They only needed someone to go first.

points.head: They pursued what they used to run from.
points.body: Same army, same enemy, brand new courage. Capacity is contagious.

points.head: Your victory raises the ceiling for everybody watching.
points.body: Somebody in your class, your street, your family is waiting to see it done once.

mirrors.ot: Deborah arose "a mother in Israel" and Barak and ten thousand followed (Judges 4:8–10; 5:7).
mirrors.nt: "When they saw the boldness of Peter and John... they took knowledge of them, that they had been with Jesus" (Acts 4:13). The credential was His company — and the whole city noticed.

days.christ: Jesus is the greater David: He went out alone on our behalf, defeated the enemy we could never face, and shares the victory with everyone standing behind Him — "Thanks be to God, which giveth us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ" (1 Corinthians 15:57). And He said, "He that believeth on me, the works that I do shall he do also" (John 14:12). He does not just win; He multiplies winners.
days.challenge: Name one person you will help stand this term. Tell them today that you believe they can.
days.prayer: Who is watching you? What are they learning is possible? (1 Samuel 17:52)
days.centralTruth: One person's courage releases a generation.
days.codeLine: Make others brave.

quiz.q: Who arose and pursued the Philistines?
options: The men of Israel and of Judah

quiz.q: What does the lesson say capacity is?
What did David's servants do, according to the echo in 2 Samuel 21:22?

days.title: Become God's Answer

scripture.text: David, after he had served his own generation by the will of God, fell on sleep

days.hook: The full board, all five panels blazing. Presenter walks into frame and stops. "Thirty days ago you were a person with potential." Beat. Looks straight down the lens. "Today you are a person with a plan."
days.story: David's capacity removed reproach → defeated an enemy → awakened an army → served a nation.

points.head: Capacity travels outward in stages.
points.body: Reproach removed → enemy defeated → army awakened → nation served. It started with one boy and one gift, developed in private.

points.head: God is not looking for the amazing. He is looking for the available.
points.body: "David, after he had served his own generation by the will of God, fell on sleep" (Acts 13:36). One sentence, one whole life: he served his generation.

points.head: You are entering 2026/2027 as an answer.
points.body: Not as a student hoping to survive the session — as somebody God has spent September preparing to use.

mirrors.ot: "God did send me before you to preserve life" (Genesis 45:5). Joseph's whole story had one purpose under it, and he only saw it at the end.
mirrors.nt: "Ye are the light of the world. A city that is set on an hill cannot be hid... Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven" (Matthew 5:14–16).

days.christ: Every SuperPower this month has one source. "I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me" (Philippians 4:13). David developed a sling; God delivered the giant. You develop your gift; God delivers the outcome. And the reason any of it matters is Him: "for of him, and through him, and to him, are all things" (Romans 11:36).
days.challenge: Stand where you are. Say your five stones out loud. Say your cause sentence out loud. Then name the one person you will help stand this term.
days.prayer: You are a city set on a hill. What will your light do in this new session? (Matthew 5:14–16)
days.centralTruth: God is not looking for the amazing. He is looking for the available.
days.codeLine: Become God's answer.

quiz.q: What is the closing question of the month?
options: What problem will my capacity solve?
